River of Life
rĭv´ẽr ŭv līf
n. phrase (the river of the water of life proceeding from the throne of God and of the Lamb; and the figure of the Spirit's supply in the believer)
The figure runs from Eden's four rivers through Ezekiel's temple stream to Revelation's crystal river, and the New Testament identifies its meaning: John says plainly that the living water spoken of is the Spirit.

See also: River of Life

Biblical Definition

The river of life is the last picture in the Bible: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb” (Rev 22:1). Ezekiel saw it rising in the temple and deepening as it ran, and its property is stated: “every thing shall live whither the river cometh” (Eze 47:9). The psalm sets it against a city under siege: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God” (Psa 46:4). The Lord makes it internal and outbound: “He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water” (John 7:38). And to the woman at the well: it “shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines river as a large stream of water flowing in a channel on land towards the ocean, a lake or another river; and notes that the fresh waters of the earth are conveyed by rivers to the ocean.

expand to see more

RIVER, n. A large stream of water flowing in a channel on land towards the ocean, a lake or another river.

It is larger than a rivulet or brook; but there are many small streams of water to which the name of river is given.

FOUNTAIN, n. A spring, or source of water; properly, a spring or issuing of water from the earth.

2. The head or source of a river.

Key Scripture

Rev 22:1 — "And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb."

Eze 47:9 — "And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live: and there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh."

Psa 46:4 — "There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High."

John 7:38 — "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water."

John 4:14 — "But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life."

Modern Corruption

The river is treated as a private supply, and every text that describes it has it running outward and reaching something dead.

expand to see more

John 7:38 has a direction that most devotional use of it reverses: out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. Not into him — through him and out. The next verse removes any doubt about what is meant: this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive. A believer is not a reservoir but a channel, and the supply is verified downstream. John 4:14 has the inward half — a well of water springing up into everlasting life — and the two together give the whole: a spring inside a man that does not stay inside him.

Ezekiel 47 is the most instructive of the passages because of what the prophet is made to do. He is measured out into the water four times — ankles, knees, loins, and then waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed over — and the man with the line asks him, Son of man, hast thou seen this? The river deepens the further it gets from its source, which is the opposite of how rivers behave and the point of the vision. And where it arrives, the salt sea, it heals; every thing shall live whither the river cometh, and the fishers stand on the banks.

Psalm 46:4 is worth setting beside those, because it is written about a city with an army outside it. There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God — and Jerusalem had no river, only the Gihon spring feeding a tunnel under the wall. That is the figure exactly: a supply that does not run past the gate where the enemy can see it, quiet and hidden and entirely sufficient, in a psalm that begins God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Revelation 22 finally shows it in the open, proceeding from the throne, with the tree of life on either side and its leaves for the healing of the nations.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek potamos (G4215), a river; hudor zon (G5204), living water; pege (G4077), a spring, well; Hebrew nachal (H5158), a stream, torrent.

expand to see more

Greek potamos hudatos zoes (G4215, G5204) — river of water of life; Revelation 22:1, and rivers, John 7:38.

Greek pege hudatos hallomenou (G4077) — a well of water springing up; John 4:14.

Hebrew nachal (H5158) — stream, torrent, wadi; Ezekiel 47:5–9, Psalm 36:8.

Usage

"“Out of his belly shall flow” — through him, and out."

"“Every thing shall live whither the river cometh” — and it ran to the salt sea."

"“There is a river” — and Jerusalem had none that anyone could see."
